question: Which of our products depend on a single-source material anywhere in their bill of materials, and how much TRx volume is at risk?
answer:
**Answer:** 49 finished goods depend on at least one single-source material somewhere in their current bill of materials. Four of them have prescription data, and together they account for **16,554 TRx in the last 13 weeks (weeks ending 2026-07-03 to 2026-09-25). That is 94.4% of our 17,540 company TRx.**

**TRx at risk (last 13 weeks)**

| Product (NDC11) | TRx | Single-source material (only qualified supplier) | BOM depth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL (99101010105) | 7,017 | CMP-310 emulsifier premix (S-201); RM-221 Polysorbate 80 low-peroxide (S-104) | 4 levels |
| Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL (99101010110) | 3,425 | Same as above | 4 levels |
| Cyclosporine OS 0.05% 5 mL (99101020205) | 3,544 | Same as above | 4 levels |
| Oculon 0.005% 2.5 mL (99101030325) | 2,568 | CMP-505 2.5 mL LDPE dropper bottle (S-150) | 2 levels |
| **Total** | **16,554** | | |

- **Not exposed:** Oculon 5 mL (986 TRx). It doesn't use the 2.5 mL dropper.
- **Lacrivia's substitute is exposed too:** Cyclosporine OS relies on the same two single-source materials as Lacrivia. Under the substitution rule (BR-SUB-01), it would not count as an approved substitute in a shortage caused by those materials. Medical Affairs would then guide therapeutic alternatives. Oculon has no company substitute. Together that is 13,986 TRx (Lacrivia plus Cyclosporine OS) with no company fallback.
- **RM-221 is easy to miss:** it has two suppliers listed, but only S-104 is qualified. Counting all listed suppliers would wrongly treat it as dual-source.
- **The other 45 finished goods have no TRx data.** They are lens care (11), surgical viscoelastic (10), eye-health supplements (2), diagnostic drops (11) and ophthalmic antibiotics (11). Together they depend on 16 of the other single-source materials, such as RM-10857, RM-10360, RM-10211, RM-11172 and CMP-50757. The commercial prescription database only covers the ophthalmic brands, so I can't put a TRx figure on these.

**Sources and definitions**
- **Supply side:** the ratified Supply Network data product in the supply warehouse. Tables used: the bill of materials (`dbo.BOM`), qualified suppliers per material (`dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL`), the material master (`dbo.MATERIAL`) and the material-to-NDC crosswalk (`dbo.MATERIAL_NDC_XREF`).
- **Demand side:** the ratified Commercial Demand data product in the commercial database. Tables used: weekly prescriptions (`PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY`) and the product master (`PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRODUCT`).
- **Linking the two:** the approved join path "Material to PackagedProduct (cross-platform)", which strips the dashes from NDCs.
- **Single-source material:** a material with exactly one qualified supplier (qualified flag = 'Y'). 24 materials qualify, and every purchased material has at least one qualified supplier.
- **Bill of materials:** only current formulations (in effect on 2026-09-30); superseded ones are excluded. I walked all levels up to the finished goods, and nothing ran deeper than the levels checked. I cross-checked the Lacrivia/Cyclosporine OS and Oculon results with the knowledge layer's supply-exposure trace, and they matched.
- **TRx:** the sum of weekly TRx over the 13 most recent weeks in the data. The legacy bill-of-materials table was not used because it is deprecated.
- **Policy:** the access check allowed this query for the SUPPLY_PLANNER role with no masking. The decision trace is logged as 87451222-6317-4b59-94b4-0ecc6d251e9b.

**Assumptions**
- "At risk" means all 13-week TRx for any pack whose supply chain includes a single-source material. It is a measure of exposure, not a forecast of lost volume. It doesn't account for inventory on hand or supplier reliability.
- A product exposed through two single-source materials (like Lacrivia) is counted once.

sql.sql:
WITH q AS (SELECT MATERIAL_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT SUPPLIER_ID) nq FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL WHERE QUALIFIED_FLG='Y' GROUP BY MATERIAL_ID),
a AS (SELECT MATERIAL_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT SUPPLIER_ID) na FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL GROUP BY MATERIAL_ID)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a) mats_with_suppliers,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM q WHERE nq=1) single_qualified,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a LEFT JOIN q ON a.MATERIAL_ID=q.MATERIAL_ID WHERE q.MATERIAL_ID IS NULL) zero_qualified,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a WHERE na=1) single_any,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.BOM WHERE EFF_TO >= '2026-09-30') cur_edges,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.BOM) all_edges

WITH cur AS (SELECT DISTINCT PARENT_MATERIAL_ID p, CHILD_MATERIAL_ID c FROM dbo.BOM WHERE EFF_TO >= '2026-09-30' AND EFF_FROM <= '2026-09-30'),
ss AS (SELECT MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL WHERE QUALIFIED_FLG='Y' GROUP BY MATERIAL_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT SUPPLIER_ID)=1),
L0 AS (SELECT MATERIAL_ID src, MATERIAL_ID node FROM ss),
L1 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L0 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L2 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L1 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L3 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L2 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L4 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L3 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L5 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L4 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L6 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L5 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L7 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L6 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L8 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L7 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L9 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L8 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L10 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L9 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L11 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L10 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L12 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L11 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
L13 AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.src, b.p node FROM L12 l JOIN cur b ON b.c=l.node),
allr AS (SELECT * FROM L1 UNION SELECT * FROM L2 UNION SELECT * FROM L3 UNION SELECT * FROM L4 UNION SELECT * FROM L5 UNION SELECT * FROM L6 UNION SELECT * FROM L7 UNION SELECT * FROM L8 UNION SELECT * FROM L9 UNION SELECT * FROM L10 UNION SELECT * FROM L11 UNION SELECT * FROM L12 UNION SELECT * FROM L13)
SELECT a.node fg, m.MATERIAL_DESC, x.NDC, COUNT(DISTINCT a.src) n_ss, STRING_AGG(a.src, ',') ss_materials,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM L13) l13_rows
FROM allr a JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=a.node LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL_NDC_XREF x ON x.MATERIAL_ID=a.node
WHERE m.MATERIAL_TYP='FG'
GROUP BY a.node, m.MATERIAL_DESC, x.NDC ORDER BY a.node

SELECT sm.MATERIAL_ID, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP, MAX(CASE WHEN sm.QUALIFIED_FLG='Y' THEN sm.SUPPLIER_ID END) qual_supplier, COUNT(*) n_supplier_rows, SUM(CASE WHEN sm.QUALIFIED_FLG='N' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_unqualified
FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=sm.MATERIAL_ID
WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID IN (SELECT MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL WHERE QUALIFIED_FLG='Y' GROUP BY MATERIAL_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT SUPPLIER_ID)=1)
GROUP BY sm.MATERIAL_ID, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP ORDER BY sm.MATERIAL_ID

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13)
SELECT p.CO_FLG, COUNT(DISTINCT p.PROD_NDC11) n_ndc, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) trx_13wk
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRODUCT p ON p.PROD_NDC11=r.PROD_NDC11
WHERE r.WK_END_DT IN (SELECT WK_END_DT FROM wk) GROUP BY 1

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13)
SELECT p.PROD_NDC11, p.BRAND_NM, p.PACK_DESC, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) trx_13wk
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRODUCT p ON p.PROD_NDC11=r.PROD_NDC11
WHERE r.WK_END_DT IN (SELECT WK_END_DT FROM wk) AND p.CO_FLG='Y' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1
